name: Linking words: and, but, or, so
subtitle: Linking words join two sentences. Use and to add, but for a contrast, or for a choice, and so for a result: I was tired, so I went to bed.

concept.exampleHtml: I'm tired, but I want to go out. · It's late, so we go home.

qa.html: These words join two sentences into one. After the linking word, write a normal sentence: subject first, then the verb. I'm hungry, but I have no time. Put a comma before but and so.

and adds: Tom cooks and I wash up. or gives a choice: Do you want tea or coffee? There is usually no comma before and and or. If the subject is the same, you can leave it out the second time: I cook and eat.
but shows a contrast: The flat is small, but it is bright. Put a comma before but when it joins two full sentences. Same subject? You can leave it out: I like tea but hate coffee.
so gives a result: It's raining, so we stay at home. The first part is the reason. The second part is the result. Put a comma before so.
because gives the reason: We stay at home because it's raining. Compare: It's raining, so we stay at home. Use so or because, never both in one sentence: ✗ Because it's raining, so we stay at home.

Typical mistakes: ✗ I stay at home, so it's raining. → ✓ …, because it's raining. · ✗ I'm hungry, but I eat a sandwich. → ✓ …, so I eat a sandwich. · ✗ I like tea, but I like coffee too. → ✓ …, and I like coffee too.

concept.noteHtml: A comma before and or or between two full sentences is allowed, but you don't need it. For the order of words in a sentence, see Word order. Questions with or are in Yes/no questions.

hoeren.instruction: Listen. Which word joins the two parts?

items.text: Would you like tea or coffee?
I have a meeting, but I can't find the office.
It's very late, so we are going home.
I clean the kitchen and my husband cleans the bathroom.
Are you coming to the cinema or are you staying at home?
The flat is small, but it is very bright.

rounds.label: 1 · Two sentences → one with but
rounds.instruction: You hear two sentences. Join them into one: comma, but, then a normal sentence.

example.prompt: The flat is nice. It is small.
example.answer: The flat is nice, but it is small.

items.prompt: I'm hungry. I have no time.
items.answer: I'm hungry, but I have no time.

items.prompt: The course is good. It starts very early.
items.answer: The course is good, but it starts very early.

items.prompt: My boss is nice. He talks very fast.
items.answer: My boss is nice, but he talks very fast.

items.prompt: The shop is open. I have no money.
items.answer: The shop is open, but I have no money.

items.prompt: I understand a lot. I speak very little.
items.answer: I understand a lot, but I speak very little.

items.prompt: The doctor is friendly. The waiting room is full.
items.answer: The doctor is friendly, but the waiting room is full.

rounds.label: 2 · The result → so
rounds.instruction: You hear two sentences. The first is the reason. Join them with so.

example.prompt: It's raining. We stay at home.
example.answer: It's raining, so we stay at home.

items.prompt: I have a headache. I go to the doctor.
items.answer: I have a headache, so I go to the doctor.

items.prompt: Our flat is small. We want a new one.
items.answer: Our flat is small, so we want a new one.

items.prompt: The bus is late. I take a taxi.
items.answer: The bus is late, so I take a taxi.

items.prompt: I want to work here. I learn English.
items.answer: I want to work here, so I learn English.

items.prompt: She is tired. She goes to bed.
items.answer: She is tired, so she goes to bed.

items.prompt: It's cold. He wears a coat.
items.answer: It's cold, so he wears a coat.

exercises.title: and, or or but?
exercises.hint: and: adds something. or: a choice. but: a contrast. There is a comma before but.
exercises.hintHtml: andAdds something: both things happen.orA choice, often in questions.butA contrast. There is a comma before it.

items.prompt: Would you like tea ___ coffee?
items.why: Tea, coffee: you choose one of them. So: or.

items.prompt: The flat is nice, ___ it is very expensive.
items.why: Nice, but expensive: that is a contrast. So: but.

items.prompt: I cook today ___ Tom washes up.
items.why: I cook, he washes up: both things happen. So: and.

items.prompt: Are you coming on Monday ___ on Tuesday?
items.why: Monday, Tuesday: only one day. So: or.

items.prompt: The doctor is nice, ___ I have to wait a long time.
items.why: Nice, but a long wait: a contrast. So: but.

items.prompt: I go to the shop ___ then I go to work.
items.why: First the shop, then work: both things happen. So: and.

items.prompt: Do you pay in cash ___ by card?
items.why: Cash, card: only one of them. So: or.

items.prompt: My son is only six, ___ he can already read.
items.why: Only six, but he can read: a contrast. So: but.

sentences.hint: It is small. + It is nice. (but)
Do you want tea? + Do you want coffee? (or — one question)
I am hungry. + I make lunch. (so)
I learn English. + I want a job. (because — the reason comes second)

exercises.title: Can you leave out the subject? Right or wrong?
exercises.hint: After and, or and but you can leave out the same subject. After so and because, the subject must stay.

rows.term: I am tired, so stay at home.
We go to the cinema or stay at home.
She is tired, because has worked all day.
He works a lot but earns little.
We are hungry, so are going to a café.

exercises.title: so or because?
exercises.hint: so: the result. because: the reason.
exercises.hintHtml: soThe result comes after it.becauseThe reason comes after it.

items.prompt: It's raining, ___ we stay at home.
items.why: Staying at home is the result of the rain. So: so.

items.prompt: We stay at home ___ it's raining.
items.why: The rain is the reason. So: because.

items.prompt: I'm hungry, ___ I make a sandwich.
items.why: The sandwich is the result of being hungry. So: so.

items.prompt: I make a sandwich ___ I'm hungry.
items.why: Being hungry is the reason. So: because.

items.prompt: The shop is closed, ___ we go home.
items.why: Going home is the result. So: so.

items.prompt: I'm learning English ___ I want to work here.
items.why: Wanting to work here is the reason. So: because.

items.prompt: She is ill, ___ she doesn't go to work.
items.why: Not going to work is the result. So: so.

items.prompt: He takes a taxi ___ he is late.
items.why: Being late is the reason. So: because.

exercises.title: What comes after because or so?
exercises.hint: After because and so, write a normal sentence: subject first, then the verb. The subject never disappears.

rows.term: I don't go to work today, because …
We want a new flat, because …
She learns English every day, because …
rows.answer: she wants to work in London
choices: she wants to work in London
wants she to work in London
she to work in London wants

rows.term: Tom is at the doctor's, because …

exercises.title: Find the mistake — how is it correct?
exercises.hint: Each sentence has one mistake: the wrong linking word or the wrong word order.

rows.term: I stay at home, so it's raining.
I'm hungry, but I eat a sandwich.
The room is small, so it is very bright.
Are you coming tonight, and are you staying at home?
rows.answer: or are you staying at home
choices: or are you staying at home
and are you staying at home
so are you staying at home
but are you staying at home

rows.term: I can't come because have I no time.
I like tea, but I like coffee too.

exercises.title: Bonus: so, because or but?
exercises.hint: so: result. because: reason. but: contrast.

items.prompt: I'm tired, ___ I'm happy.
I'm tired, ___ I go to bed.
I go to bed ___ I'm tired.
It's sunny, ___ it's cold.
It's sunny, ___ we go to the park.
We go to the park ___ it's sunny.
